title: Effective Population Size and Its Relationship with Inbreeding in the Peruvian Paso Horse
content: Objective: This study aimed to estimate the effective population size (Ne) and assess its relationship with inbreeding in the Peruvian Paso Horse, an emblematic native breed of Peru. Methods: Pedigree records from 40,993 registered animals, documented between 1938 and 2022 by the National Association of Breeders and Owners of the Peruvian Paso Horse, were analyzed using genealogical methods. Key parameters including inbreeding coefficients, rate of inbreeding, generation intervals, and Ne were estimated based on pedigree data. Pedigree structure was visualized and analyzed using the PopRep service provided by the Department of Animal Breeding and Genetics, Institute of Farm Animal Genetics.Results: A progressive increase in average inbreeding was observed over time, together with a decline in effective population size (Ne) despite continued demographic growth. Average inbreeding values exceeded 9%, and the rate of inbreeding increased markedly in recent years, indicating accelerated loss of genetic diversity.The average generation interval was 8.9 years, with slightly longer values for males than females. The distribution of reproductive and selected offspring revealed highly unequal genetic contributions, particularly through the paternal line, consistent with the accumulation of inbreeding and reduced Ne observed. Pedigree completeness exceeded 90% in recent cohorts, ensuring reliable estimation of inbreeding and effective population size. Minor reductions in the most recent years were attributed to incomplete records rather than genetic loss.Conclusion: Demographic expansion in the Peruvian Paso Horse has not been accompanied by a proportional increase in effective genetic diversity. These findings underscore the need for ongoing monitoring of inbreeding and Ne and can inform future breeding strategies aimed at ensuring the long-term genetic sustainability of the breed.
